name: fresh-review
description: Understand-first code review with enforced producer/reviewer context separation. Every run starts by explaining the change from the code alone, at a high level for someone new to the project — what this part of the system is, what the user sees or what the system now does differently, how it fits, a UML class diagram and a sequence diagram, and the alternatives — then checks with open questions that you know what the change is (not a yes/no approval, and not a hunt for bugs) before it reviews the implementation (--understood skips the check). The implementation review runs context-isolated subagents against one shared diff packet: a fast implementation pass and the gstack security audit always, the lattice review only when the feature has a lattice design or context doc, and a background cross-model Codex pass on request (--codex) or on high-risk diffs. Every finding prints the code it wants to change as a diff, a finding blocks only with a concrete failure scenario, and the report lists every comment and docstring the change adds, to drop. When the review subject has a PR, it gathers the PR description and discussion for producer-side triage — never for the blind passes — and verifies that static-analysis findings (Wiz, Snyk, SonarCloud, CodeQL, …) were fixed, suppressed, or dismissed. PR mode adds a low/med/high risk class. gstack's /review army runs only on someone else's PR and only with --army; on your own branch /ship runs it, and a dispatch gate trims what this run already covered. A stack mode plans the reviews of a PR stack and prints one handoff per review for you to run in a new session, then tracks the stack verdict. PR reviews and stack units support a re-review (--delta) of only what changed since the last review, which checks each earlier blocker.
